intro: Levar means to take or carry something or someone away from where you are, towards somewhere else. It's a regular -ar verb and also means 'to take (time)': Leva uma hora.

presente.pt: Eu [levo] o meu filho à escola todos os dias.
presente.en: I take my son to school every day.
Are you taking the umbrella? It's going to rain.

presente.pt: O autocarro [leva] vinte minutos até ao centro.
presente.en: The bus takes twenty minutes to the centre.

presente.pt: Nós [levamos] o vinho para o jantar.
presente.en: We'll bring the wine to the dinner.

presente.pt: Vocês [levam] o cão para a praia?
presente.en: Do you take the dog to the beach?

perfeito.en: I took the car to the garage yesterday.
He took his girlfriend to the cinema.
They took a long time to decide.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era pequeno, [levava] sempre um livro para a praia.
imperfeito.en: When I was little, I always took a book to the beach.

imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe [levava]-nos à escola de carro.
imperfeito.en: My mother used to take us to school by car.
We used to bring lunch from home.

imperfeito.pt: Os meus avós [levavam] uma vida simples.
imperfeito.en: My grandparents led a simple life.

futuro.en: I'll bring the dessert.
Will you take your brother to the party?

futuro.pt: Nós [levaremos] os miúdos ao jardim zoológico.
futuro.en: We will take the kids to the zoo.
They will carry everything in the car.

condicional.pt: Eu [levaria] um casaco, se fosse a ti.
condicional.en: I would take a coat, if I were you.

condicional.pt: [Levarias] esta carta aos correios, por favor?
condicional.en: Would you take this letter to the post office, please?
By train, he would take longer.
Would you take the dog on holiday?

presente.en: I take the children to school.
A coffee to take away, please.
presente.pt: Um café para levar, por favor.

perfeito.en: We took the dog to the vet.

imperfeito.en: My father used to take me to football.
imperfeito.pt: O meu pai levava-me ao futebol.

imperfeito.en: We always took too many clothes.
She used to carry a big bag.

futuro.en: I'm going to take you home.
Are you going to take the car?
It will take a long time.

condicional.en: I would take the car.
Would you take me to the airport?
That would take a week.

notes.presente: Levar = take/carry away from where the speaker is; trazer = bring towards the speaker. Levar also means 'to take (time)': Leva uma hora. Levar tempo a + infinitivo: Levo tempo a acordar.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: levámos (Brazil: levamos).
notes.imperfeito: Levar uma vida + adjective = to lead a ... life: levava uma vida calma.
notes.futuro: In speech, use ir + infinitivo: vou levar, vamos levar. With a pronoun: vou levar-te.
notes.condicional: In everyday European Portuguese the imperfeito often replaces the condicional in requests: Levavas-me ao aeroporto?

patterns.en: to take time to do something

compare.ex: Podes trazer o pão para casa?
Tomo um café depois do almoço.

compare.en: to take out / to take off

recap: Levo o guarda-chuva para o trabalho e trago-o de volta para casa. (I take the umbrella to work and bring it back home.)

intro: Trazer means to bring something or someone towards where the speaker is. It's irregular: trago, traz, trouxe, trarei. Use it whenever something comes here, to you.

presente.en: Are you bringing the phone charger?

perfeito.en: I brought a present for you.
She brought her children to the party.

imperfeito.pt: Antigamente, [trazia] sempre um livro na mala.
imperfeito.en: I used to always carry a book in my bag.

imperfeito.pt: O meu pai [trazia]-nos chocolates das viagens.
imperfeito.en: My father used to bring us chocolates from his trips.
We used to bring water to the beach.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [traziam] o jornal todas as manhãs.
imperfeito.en: They brought the newspaper every morning.

futuro.en: I'll bring the wine.
The postman will bring the parcel tomorrow.
We'll bring the photos from the trip.
Will you bring the kids?

condicional.pt: Eu [traria] mais comida, mas não havia espaço.
condicional.en: I would bring more food, but there was no room.
Would you bring your guitar?
He would bring the car, if he could.
They would bring everything, if we asked them.

presente.en: Can you bring me the menu?
What are you bringing to the party?
presente.pt: O que trazes para a festa?

imperfeito.en: She always brought sweets.
We used to bring our lunch.
My grandmother used to bring me books.

futuro.en: I'm going to bring the dessert.
Are you going to bring your sister?
They will bring the chairs.

condicional.en: Would you bring me a glass of water?
I would bring more, but I can't.
That would bring problems.

notes.presente: Irregular: eu trago, ele traz (no final -e). Trazer = towards the speaker ('here'); levar = away from the speaker ('there').
notes.perfeito: The whole perfeito is irregular: trouxe, trouxeste, trouxe... The x sounds like 'ss': 'trôsse'. Eu and ele share the form trouxe.
notes.futuro: Futuro and condicional drop -ze-: trarei, traria (like fazer → farei, dizer → direi). In speech: vou trazer.
notes.condicional: For polite requests, the imperfeito is common in EP: Trazias-me um copo de água?

compare.ex: Levo o lixo lá para fora.

recap: Quando vieres, traz o pão e eu levo o vinho. (When you come, bring the bread and I'll take the wine.)

intro: Começar means to start or begin. It's a regular -ar verb with one spelling change: ç becomes c before e (comecei). Use começar a + infinitive for starting an action.

presente.en: When do you start the new job?
We always start with a soup.

perfeito.pt: [Comecei] a estudar português no ano passado.
perfeito.en: I started studying Portuguese last year.
Have you started the book yet?
We started the meeting without him.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [começava] o dia com um café.
imperfeito.en: I used to start the day with a coffee.
The class always started late.
We used to start dinner at eight.
When I arrived, they were starting to tidy up.

futuro.en: I'll start tomorrow.
You'll start on Monday.

futuro.pt: O concerto [começará] com meia hora de atraso.
futuro.en: The concert will start half an hour late.
We'll start by cleaning the kitchen.

condicional.en: I would start earlier, if I could.
Where would you start?

condicional.pt: Nós [começaríamos] já, mas falta o chefe.
condicional.en: We would start now, but the boss isn't here.
They would start the building work in May.

presente.en: What time does the class start?
presente.pt: A que horas começa a aula?

imperfeito.en: It was starting to get dark.
I was starting to get tired.
The parties always started late.

futuro.en: I'm going to start tomorrow.
The game is going to start soon.
futuro.pt: O jogo vai começar daqui a pouco.

futuro.en: We'll start from scratch.

condicional.en: I would start with the soup.
Would you start again?
It would start at six.

notes.presente: Começar a + infinitivo = to start doing: começo a trabalhar. Começar por + infinitivo = to start by doing.
notes.perfeito: Spelling change: comecei (ç → c before e), but começaste, começou. European spelling: começámos (Brazil: começamos).
notes.imperfeito: Começou a chover = it started to rain (once). Começava a chover = it was starting to rain (background).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou começar, vamos começar.

patterns.en: to start with / first of all

compare.ex: A reunião vai iniciar-se às dez.

recap: Comecei a aprender português e agora não quero parar! (I started learning Portuguese and now I don't want to stop!)

intro: Acabar means to finish or to end. It's a regular -ar verb with very useful patterns: acabar de + infinitive (to have just done) and acabar com (to put an end to / to break up with).

presente.en: What time do you finish work?

imperfeito.en: I had just left when you called.

imperfeito.pt: O jantar [acabava] sempre com um café.
imperfeito.en: Dinner always ended with a coffee.
We used to finish classes at five.
The films always ended well.

futuro.en: I'll finish the course in June.
Take it easy, you'll finish on time.
This will end badly.
The building work will end in March.

condicional.en: I would finish today, if I had help.
Would you finish this for me?
That way, the problem would end.
We would finish earlier without meetings.

presente.pt: Estou a acabar o meu café.

perfeito.en: Have you finished? Yes, I've finished.

imperfeito.en: We had just arrived.
The day always ended at the beach.
imperfeito.pt: O dia acabava sempre na praia.

imperfeito.en: I used to finish work at six.

futuro.en: I'm going to finish this today.
It's going to end well.
When are you going to finish?

condicional.en: I would finish sooner.
That would end the discussion.
Would they finish on time?

notes.presente: Acabar de + infinitivo = to have just done: Acabo de chegar (I've just arrived). Acabar por + infinitivo = to end up doing.
notes.perfeito: Acabou! = it's over / it's run out. Acabar com alguém = to break up with someone. European spelling: acabámos.
notes.imperfeito: Acabava de + infinitivo = had just done: Acabava de sair quando ligaste.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou acabar, vai acabar.

patterns.en: to put an end to / to break up with

recap: Acabo de acabar o trabalho! (I've just finished work!)

intro: Parecer means to seem, to look (like) or to appear. It's a regular -er verb with one spelling change: pareço (c → ç before o). It's very often used impersonally: parece que..., parece-me que...

presente.en: This looks easy, but it isn't.
With this map, we look like tourists.

perfeito.en: Did I seem nervous in the interview?
Yesterday you seemed worried to me.
The film seemed very long to me.
The questions seemed difficult to me.

imperfeito.en: The house looked bigger in the photos.
When I was young, I looked older.
We looked lost.
They seemed happy.

futuro.pt: Daqui a uns meses, isto [parecerá] normal.
futuro.en: In a few months, this will seem normal.
With that hat, you'll look like a tourist.
With these clothes, we'll look Portuguese.
The first days will seem difficult.

condicional.en: That would seem strange.

condicional.pt: Com estes sapatos, eu [pareceria] mais alto.
condicional.en: With these shoes, I would look taller.
Without a beard, you would look younger.
They would seem friendlier, if they smiled.

presente.en: It seems that it's going to rain.
I think so. (It seems so to me.)

imperfeito.en: He seemed sad.
It looked like a good idea.
You seemed happy.

futuro.en: It's going to look strange.
It will seem easy later.
You'll look like a local.

condicional.en: That would seem rude.
It would look better in blue.
Would I look older?

notes.presente: Spelling: pareço (c → ç before o). Very common impersonal uses: Parece que... (it seems that...), Parece-me que... (I think that...). To resemble someone use parecer-se com: Pareço-me com o meu pai.
notes.perfeito: Pareceu-me (it seemed to me) is a soft way to give an opinion. Note nós parecemos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito describes how things looked in the past: Parecia cansado (he looked tired).
notes.futuro: In speech: vai parecer (it's going to seem).

patterns.en: I think that... / it seems to me that...

compare.ex: Pareço-me muito com a minha mãe.

recap: Parece difícil, mas parece-me que vais conseguir. (It looks difficult, but I think you'll manage.)

intro: Tornar-se means to become. The endings are regular -ar, but the verb is always used with a reflexive pronoun (torno-me, tornas-te, torna-se...), so you have to learn where the pronoun goes. It's used for real changes: becoming a doctor, friends, famous or difficult.

quick.pt: Isto está a tornar-se um problema.

presente.en: When I'm nervous, I become very quiet.
Over time, you become more confident.

presente.pt: O português [torna]-se mais fácil com a prática.

presente.en: With age, we become more patient.

perfeito.en: I became a teacher five years ago.
They became famous with this song.

imperfeito.en: The weather was getting worse and worse.
When I was alone, I used to become sad.
In the heat, we used to get lazy.
At night, the streets became dangerous.

futuro.en: I don't think I'll ever become rich.

futuro.pt: Se estudares, sei que [te tornarás] fluente.
futuro.en: If you study, I know you'll become fluent.
He says he will become a pilot.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [nos tornaremos] bons amigos.
futuro.en: I'm sure we'll become good friends.

condicional.pt: Sem ti, não [me tornaria] o que sou.
condicional.en: Without you, I wouldn't become who I am.

condicional.pt: Achei que o problema não [se tornaria] tão grave.
condicional.en: I thought the problem wouldn't become so serious.
I never thought we would become neighbours.

condicional.pt: Eu sabia que eles [se tornariam] amigos.
condicional.en: I knew they would become friends.

presente.pt: A vida está a tornar-se mais cara.

presente.en: I want to become a doctor.

imperfeito.en: It was becoming difficult.
The days were getting shorter.
He used to get aggressive easily.

futuro.en: It's going to become a problem.
You're going to become a great teacher.
I don't think it will become easier.
futuro.pt: Acho que não se vai tornar mais fácil.

condicional.en: It would become too expensive.
I knew she would become a doctor.
condicional.pt: Sabia que ela se tornaria médica.

condicional.en: Nobody thought it would become so popular.
condicional.pt: Ninguém pensou que se tornaria tão popular.

notes.presente: In affirmative main clauses the pronoun goes after the verb: torna-se. After não, que, quando, nunca etc. it goes before: não se torna. Note the nós form loses its -s: tornamos + nos → tornamo-nos. For everyday changes of state, ficar is more common: fiquei cansado (I got tired).
notes.perfeito: European spelling: tornámo-nos (Brazil: nós nos tornamos). Tornar-se + noun for professions and relationships: tornou-se médica, tornaram-se amigos.
notes.imperfeito: Tornava-se cada vez mais... = was getting more and more... (a gradual change in the past).
notes.futuro: The table shows the written form, with the pronoun in the middle (tornar-me-ei, tornar-se-á). It sounds very formal. After não, que, nunca the pronoun goes in front: não me tornarei. In speech use ir + infinitivo: vou tornar-me, vai tornar-se.
notes.condicional: Like the futuro: after que, não etc. say se tornaria. Standing alone, formal written EP uses tornar-se-ia.

compare.en: to become / to get (a change of state)
compare.ex: Fiquei muito contente com a notícia.

recap: O sonho tornou-se realidade: tornei-me professor! (The dream came true: I became a teacher!)

intro: Sair means to go out, to leave or to exit a place. It's irregular: the i of the stem keeps showing up (saio, sai, saímos), and several forms need an accent. Use sair de for the place you leave and sair com for going out with someone.

presente.en: What time do you leave work?

presente.pt: O comboio [sai] da estação às dez.
presente.en: The train leaves the station at ten.

presente.pt: Nós [saímos] com os amigos ao sábado.
presente.en: We go out with friends on Saturdays.
Do you go out a lot at night?

perfeito.en: I left the office very late.
Who did you go out with yesterday?
They left the restaurant without paying.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era estudante, [saía] todas as noites.
imperfeito.en: When I was a student, I went out every night.
He was leaving when I arrived.
We always used to go out together.
They never left the house.

futuro.en: I'll leave earlier tomorrow.
The next bus will leave at nine.
We'll go out after dinner.
The results will come out on Friday.

condicional.en: I would go out, but it's raining.
Would you go out with him?
We would go out more, if we had money.
They would never leave without saying.

presente.en: Do you go out on Fridays?

perfeito.en: I left home without my keys.
perfeito.pt: Saí de casa sem as chaves.

imperfeito.en: We used to go out a lot.
She never went out at night.
I was leaving when you called.

futuro.en: I'm going to go out tonight.
When are you going to leave?
The plane will leave at six.
futuro.pt: O avião vai sair às seis.

condicional.en: I wouldn't go out in this rain.
condicional.pt: Eu não sairia com esta chuva.

condicional.en: Would you go out with me?
It would be better to leave early.

notes.presente: Irregular: saio, sais, sai, saímos, saem. Sair de = to leave a place (saio de casa); sair com = to go out with; sair-se bem = to do well.
notes.perfeito: Watch the accents: saí, saíste, saímos, saíram – but saiu. They show that a and i are pronounced separately.
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito always has an accent on the í: saía, saías, saíamos.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou sair (I'm going out), vamos sair.

compare.en: to leave / to depart (on a journey)

recap: Saí de casa às oito e entrei no escritório às nove. (I left home at eight and went into the office at nine.)

intro: Entrar means to enter or to go/come in. It's a regular -ar verb. In Portuguese you enter 'in' something: entrar em (no, na, nos, nas).

presente.en: Are you coming in or staying outside?
The sun comes in through the window.
We go in through the front door.

presente.pt: As crianças [entram] na escola aos seis anos.

perfeito.pt: [Entrei] na loja para ver os preços.
perfeito.en: I went into the shop to see the prices.
We got on the wrong train.
The thieves came in through the window.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [entrava] sempre pela porta das traseiras.
imperfeito.en: I always used to go in through the back door.
Whenever he came in, everyone went quiet.
We used to get into the beach for free.
They were coming in when I left.

futuro.en: I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.
With these grades, you'll get into university.

futuro.pt: A lei [entrará] em vigor em janeiro.
futuro.en: The law will come into force in January.
We'll go in through the other door.

condicional.en: I wouldn't go into that restaurant.
Would you go into a haunted house?

condicional.pt: Ele [entraria], mas tem medo do cão.
condicional.en: He would come in, but he's afraid of the dog.

condicional.pt: Vocês [entrariam] na água com este frio?
condicional.en: Would you go into the water in this cold?

imperfeito.en: Nobody used to come in.
I used to start school at eight.
The cat always came in through the window.
imperfeito.pt: O gato entrava sempre pela janela.

futuro.en: I'm going to go in.
We're going to get in touch.
Are you going to come in?

condicional.en: I wouldn't go in there.
Would you go into the sea?
They would come in, but it's closed.

notes.presente: Entrar takes em: entro no carro, entramos na loja. To 'get on' a bus or train in EP you can say entrar no autocarro (or apanhar o autocarro for 'catch').
notes.perfeito: European spelling: entrámos (Brazil: entramos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou entrar. Entrar em contacto com = to get in touch with (EP spelling contacto).

patterns.en: to come in through the door

recap: Entrei no café, pedi uma bica e saí feliz. (I went into the café, ordered an espresso and came out happy.)

intro: Voltar means to return, to come back or to go back. It's a regular -ar verb. With a + infinitive it means to do something again: volto a ligar (I'll call again).

presente.en: I go back home at six.
When are you back from holiday?

presente.pt: Nós [voltamos] a Lisboa todos os verões.
presente.en: We go back to Lisbon every summer.

perfeito.en: I got back from Porto last night.
Did you talk to her again?
We came back late from the party.

imperfeito.pt: Todos os anos, [voltava] à aldeia dos meus avós.
imperfeito.en: Every year I went back to my grandparents' village.
He always came back with presents.
We used to walk back from school.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [voltavam] para casa quando começou a chover.
imperfeito.en: They were going back home when it started to rain.

futuro.en: I'll be back soon.
I'm sure you'll come back.

futuro.pt: O bom tempo [voltará] na próxima semana.
futuro.en: The good weather will return next week.
Will you come back next year?

condicional.en: I would come back to this hotel.
Would you go back to living in Portugal?
He said he would be back at five.
We would come back tomorrow, if it were possible.

perfeito.en: We went back to the restaurant.

imperfeito.en: I used to come back late.
He always came back on Sundays.
We were coming back from the beach.

futuro.en: I'm going to call again.
We're going to come back next year.
Are you going to come back?

condicional.en: I would go back.
Would you do it again?
They said they would come back.

notes.presente: Voltar a + infinitivo = to do again: Volto a ligar (I'll call again). Voltar para = go back to (for longer, e.g. home); voltar a = go back to (a place, a visit).
notes.perfeito: European spelling: voltámos (Brazil: voltamos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou voltar, vamos voltar. Para o ano = next year (common in EP).
notes.condicional: Disse que voltaria = he said he would come back (reported speech).

patterns.en: to go back / to change one's mind

compare.ex: Tenho de devolver o livro à biblioteca.

recap: Gostei tanto de Lisboa que vou voltar para o ano. (I liked Lisbon so much that I'm going back next year.)

intro: Achar is the everyday verb for giving an opinion: Acho que... (I think that...). It's a regular -ar verb. It can also mean to find something to be a certain way: Acho o filme aborrecido.

presente.en: I think it's going to rain.
What do you think of this dress?

presente.pt: Nós [achamos] que é uma boa ideia.
presente.en: We think it's a good idea.

perfeito.en: I thought the film was very good.
What did you think of the dinner?

imperfeito.en: I thought you were Spanish.
Did you think I wasn't coming?
He thought he was right.
We used to think the neighbourhood was dangerous.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [acharás] Lisboa linda.
futuro.en: I'm sure you'll find Lisbon beautiful.

futuro.pt: Daqui a uns anos, [acharei] isto engraçado.
futuro.en: In a few years, I'll find this funny.
What will your mother think?
They'll find it strange.

condicional.en: I wouldn't find that normal.
Would you find it strange if I went?
He would find this funny.
We would think it better to wait.

perfeito.en: What did you think of the film?

imperfeito.en: I thought you were at home.
She thought it was too late.
imperfeito.pt: Ela achava que era tarde demais.

imperfeito.en: We thought it was easy.

futuro.en: You're going to find it funny.
They're going to think it's strange.
I think you'll like it.

condicional.en: Would you think it's strange?
I would think it better to stay.
She would find it funny.

notes.presente: Achar que = to think (an opinion): Acho que sim. It's the most common way to give an opinion in EP. For finding a lost object, Portugal prefers encontrar.
notes.perfeito: Achei = I thought (a reaction to something specific): Achei o filme ótimo. European spelling: achámos.
notes.imperfeito: Achava que... = I thought (wrongly) that...: Achava que eras espanhol.
notes.futuro: In speech: vais achar (you'll find / think).

recap: Acho que vais achar Lisboa linda. (I think you'll find Lisbon beautiful.)

intro: Existir means to exist. It's a regular -ir verb. In everyday speech, há (there is / there are) is more common, but existe is used for emphasis or in more formal language.

presente.en: Is there a café near here?
Do shops like that still exist?
As far as they're concerned, I don't exist.
So you do exist! You never answer messages.

perfeito.pt: Os dinossauros [existiram] há milhões de anos.
perfeito.en: Dinosaurs existed millions of years ago.
As a company, we only existed for two years.

imperfeito.en: There used to be a factory here.
In the old days there were no mobile phones.
We existed before the Internet too!

imperfeito.pt: Antes de te conhecer, [existias] só nos meus sonhos.
imperfeito.en: Before I met you, you only existed in my dreams.

futuro.pt: Daqui a cem anos, ainda [existirá] papel?
futuro.en: In a hundred years, will paper still exist?
Books will always exist.
For me, you will always exist.
As a team, we'll exist as long as there are players.

condicional.en: Without water, life wouldn't exist.
Without you, these books wouldn't exist.

condicional.pt: Sem a minha mãe, eu não [existiria].
condicional.en: Without my mother, I wouldn't exist.

condicional.pt: Sem os nossos avós, nós não [existiríamos].
condicional.en: Without our grandparents, we wouldn't exist.

presente.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?

imperfeito.en: There used to be a cinema here.
Computers didn't exist.
There was a small problem.

futuro.en: Will it still exist?
There will always be differences.
The shop won't exist next year.
futuro.pt: A loja não vai existir para o ano.

condicional.en: Without music, life wouldn't exist.
condicional.pt: Sem música, a vida não existiria.

condicional.en: That would not exist without you.
Would there be a solution?

notes.presente: Existir agrees with what exists: existe um problema, existem dois problemas. Haver doesn't change: há um problema, há dois problemas. In speech, há is more common.
notes.perfeito: Note nós existimos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Existia / existiam = there was / there were (in the background): Antigamente não existiam telemóveis.
notes.futuro: In speech: vai existir, vão existir.

compare.ex: Há um café ali ao fundo.
O café está ali ao fundo.

recap: Os dinossauros existiram, mas os dragões nunca existiram. (Dinosaurs existed, but dragons never did.)

intro: Sentir means to feel or to sense. It has a stem change in the eu form of the presente (sinto); everything else is regular. Use sentir + noun (sinto frio) and sentir-se + adjective (sinto-me bem).

presente.en: From here we can smell the sea.

perfeito.pt: Ontem à noite [senti] um tremor de terra.
perfeito.en: Last night I felt an earthquake.
Did you feel the cold outside?
She felt ill on the bus.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I was afraid of the dark.
He felt lonely in Lisbon.

imperfeito.pt: [Sentíamos] o calor do sol na cara.
imperfeito.en: We could feel the heat of the sun on our faces.
They missed their family.

futuro.en: After the coffee, you'll feel more energy.
Tomorrow my legs will ache.
She will feel the difference.

futuro.pt: Os turistas [sentirão] o calor de agosto.
futuro.en: The tourists will feel the August heat.

condicional.en: I would miss the sea.
How would you feel in my place?
We would miss you very much.
Without a coat, they would feel cold.

perfeito.en: He felt a pain in his back.
perfeito.pt: Ele sentiu uma dor nas costas.

imperfeito.en: I felt at home.
She was always cold.
We felt happy.

futuro.en: You're going to feel better.
We're going to miss you.
You'll feel the difference.

condicional.en: I think I would feel strange.
How would you feel?
She would miss the city.
condicional.pt: Ela sentiria a falta da cidade.

notes.presente: Only eu changes: sinto (e → i), like preferir → prefiro and vestir → visto. Sentir + noun: sinto frio, sinto fome. Sentir-se + adjective: sinto-me bem, sinto-me cansado.
notes.perfeito: To miss someone: sentir a falta de or ter saudades de. Sinto muito = I'm so sorry. Nós sentimos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Sentia-me... describes how you felt over a period: Sentia-me sozinho (I felt lonely).
notes.futuro: In speech: vais sentir-te melhor (you'll feel better).

compare.en: to think / to feel (that), an opinion

recap: Sinto frio, mas sinto-me feliz. (I'm cold, but I feel happy.)

intro: Chamar means to call someone (with your voice) or to call something by a name. It's a regular -ar verb. Its reflexive form chamar-se gives you one of the first phrases you learn: Chamo-me... (My name is...).

presente.en: In Lisbon, we call an espresso a bica.

perfeito.en: I called a taxi to the airport.
The doctor called the next patient.

imperfeito.en: My grandfather was called António.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [chamava] o meu irmão para jantar.
imperfeito.en: I used to call my brother for dinner.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [chamávamos] o cão, mas ele não vinha.
imperfeito.en: We called the dog, but he wouldn't come.
My friends used to call me Zé.

futuro.en: I'll call a taxi for eight o'clock.
The receptionist will call your name.
Will you call the doctor if it gets worse?
We'll call the technician tomorrow.

condicional.en: I would call the police.
Would you call a taxi for me?

condicional.pt: Ele não [chamaria] a isso um jantar.
condicional.en: He wouldn't call that a dinner.
We would call the doctor.

imperfeito.en: What was the restaurant called?
They used to call me Nico.
The street was called Rua Nova.

futuro.en: I'm going to call a taxi.
We're going to call the doctor.
What are you going to call the baby?

condicional.en: Would you call the waiter?
I would call it a disaster.
condicional.pt: Eu chamaria a isso um desastre.

condicional.en: Who would call at this hour?

notes.presente: Chamar-se = to be called: Chamo-me Ana. The pronoun goes after the verb in statements (chamo-me) but before it in questions with a question word (como te chamas?) and after não (não me chamo Ana). For phone calls, use ligar: Ligo-te amanhã.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: chamámos (Brazil: chamamos).
notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito for old names: Como se chamava o teu professor?
notes.futuro: In speech: vou chamar. Chamar a + something = to call it (a name): Como vais chamar ao bebé?

patterns.en: to be called / to be named
to call the police / the doctor
to attract attention / to tell someone off

recap: Chamo-me Ana, mas os meus amigos chamam-me Aninhas. (My name is Ana, but my friends call me Aninhas.)

intro: Considerar means to consider, to think about or to regard someone or something as. It's a regular -ar verb, a little more formal than pensar or achar.

presente.pt: Eu [considero] o Pedro um bom amigo.
presente.en: I consider Pedro a good friend.

presente.pt: Muitos [consideram] o Porto a cidade mais bonita do país.
presente.en: Many people regard Porto as the most beautiful city in the country.

perfeito.en: Have you ever considered studying abroad?
The jury considered the project excellent.

imperfeito.en: I used to consider him my best friend.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [considerava] o futebol a coisa mais importante.
imperfeito.en: He regarded football as the most important thing.
We thought the idea was good.

imperfeito.pt: Os meus pais [consideravam] a música uma perda de tempo.
imperfeito.en: My parents considered music a waste of time.

futuro.en: I'll consider your proposal.
The company will consider all candidates.
We'll consider other solutions.

futuro.pt: Eles [considerarão] o pedido na próxima semana.
futuro.en: They'll consider the request next week.

condicional.en: I would consider that option.
Would you consider living in Porto?
He would never consider that.

condicional.pt: Vocês [considerariam] trabalhar ao fim de semana?
condicional.en: Would you consider working at the weekend?

presente.pt: Estamos a considerar mudar de casa.

imperfeito.en: I considered it impossible.
She regarded him as a brother.
We thought it was too expensive.

futuro.en: I'm going to consider it.
Are you going to consider the offer?
We'll consider it tomorrow.

condicional.en: Would you consider it?
I would never consider that.
They would consider a lower price.
condicional.pt: Eles considerariam um preço mais baixo.

notes.presente: Considerar + person/thing + noun/adjective = to regard as: Considero-o inteligente. In casual speech, pensar em is more common: Estou a pensar em mudar de casa.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: considerámos (Brazil: consideramos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou considerar. The synthetic future (considerarei) sounds formal, e.g. in business letters.

compare.ex: Estou a pensar em mudar de emprego.

recap: Considero o português uma língua bonita. (I consider Portuguese a beautiful language.)

en: to put / to place / to set
intro: Pôr means to put, to place or to set. It's one of the most irregular verbs in Portuguese (ponho, pões, pus, pôs, punha) and belongs to the -er group. Keep the accent on pôr to tell it apart from the preposition por.

quick.en: Where did you put the keys?

presente.en: I put sugar in my coffee.
Where do you put the keys?

presente.pt: Ela [põe] a mesa para o jantar.
presente.en: She sets the table for dinner.
We put the clothes in the machine.
They put loud music on on Saturdays.

perfeito.en: I put the milk in the fridge.
Where did you put my phone?
He put his coat on and left.
We put the suitcases in the car.

imperfeito.pt: Eu [punha] sempre o despertador para as sete.
imperfeito.en: I always used to set the alarm for seven.

imperfeito.pt: A minha avó [punha] muito sal na comida.
imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to put a lot of salt in the food.
We used to leave our shoes by the door.
They used to put flowers in the window.

futuro.pt: [Porei] o bolo no forno às seis.
futuro.en: I'll put the cake in the oven at six.
Will you wear the blue dress?
The waiter will set the table.
We'll put the sofa there.

condicional.en: I would put the picture on this wall.
Where would you put the TV?
He would never put ketchup on salt cod.
They would put more light in the living room.

presente.en: Where do you put the plates?

perfeito.en: Where did you put my glasses?
I put the keys on the table.
perfeito.pt: Pus as chaves em cima da mesa.

imperfeito.en: We used to set the table together.
He always put music on.
I used to put milk in my tea.

futuro.en: I'm going to put the kettle on.
futuro.pt: Vou pôr a água a ferver.

futuro.en: Where are you going to put the sofa?
We're going to put the bags in the car.
futuro.pt: Vamos pôr as malas no carro.

condicional.en: Where would you put it?
I would put more salt in.
She would put the plant by the window.
condicional.pt: Ela poria a planta ao pé da janela.

notes.presente: Very irregular: ponho, pões, põe, pomos, põem. The infinitive keeps its accent (pôr) so it isn't confused with por. Pôr a mesa = to set the table; pôr-se = to set (the sun): o sol põe-se.
notes.perfeito: Eu pus, ele pôs (with accent). Pôr also means 'to put on' clothes: pôs o casaco.
notes.imperfeito: Accent only on nós: púnhamos. The rest: punha, punhas, punham.
notes.futuro: Futuro and condicional are built on por- without an accent: porei, poria. In speech: vou pôr.

compare.ex: Coloque o cartão aqui, por favor.

compare.en: to put in / inside (very common in EP)
to take out / to take off

recap: Pus as chaves na mesa, mas agora não sei onde as pus! (I put the keys on the table, but now I don't know where I put them!)

intro: Tirar means to take out, take off or remove. It's a regular -ar verb with lots of everyday uses: tirar uma fotografia (take a photo), tirar férias (take a holiday), tirar a carta (get your driving licence).

presente.pt: Eu [tiro] os sapatos quando chego a casa.
presente.en: I take my shoes off when I get home.
Will you take a photo of us?
He takes his coat off and sits down.
We take our holidays in August.

perfeito.pt: [Tirei] a carta de condução no ano passado.
perfeito.en: I got my driving licence last year.
Have you taken the cake out of the oven?
The dentist took out one of my teeth.
We took lots of photos in Sintra.

imperfeito.en: At school I always got good grades.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [tirava] o chapéu para cumprimentar.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to take off his hat to say hello.
We used to take photos of everything.

imperfeito.pt: Os padeiros [tiravam] o pão do forno às seis.
imperfeito.en: The bakers took the bread out of the oven at six.

futuro.pt: [Tirarei] uns dias de folga em maio.
futuro.en: I'll take a few days off in May.
You'll finish the degree in three years.

futuro.pt: O professor [tirará] as dúvidas na aula.
futuro.en: The teacher will answer questions in class.

futuro.pt: Eles [tirarão] os móveis da sala amanhã.
futuro.en: They'll take the furniture out of the living room tomorrow.

condicional.en: I'd take a holiday right now!
Would you take a photo with us?
He would get a good grade if he studied.
We would take the car out, but it's broken down.

presente.en: Can you take a photo of us?
She takes the money out of her wallet.
presente.pt: Ela tira o dinheiro da carteira.

perfeito.en: I took a lot of photos.

imperfeito.en: He always took his shoes off.
I used to get bad grades.
We used to take the bread out of the oven.

futuro.en: I'm going to take a photo.
Are you going to take a holiday?
She's going to get her driving licence.

condicional.en: I would take that off.
Would you take a photo?
That would take the pain away.

notes.presente: Tirar covers many English verbs: take off (tirar o casaco), take out (tirar da mala), take a photo (tirar uma fotografia), get a grade (tirar boa nota), get a licence or degree (tirar a carta, tirar um curso).
notes.perfeito: European spelling: tirámos (Brazil: tiramos). EP prefers tirar a carta for getting a driving licence.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou tirar, vais tirar.
notes.condicional: In everyday EP the imperfeito often replaces the condicional: Eu tirava isso (I'd take that off).

patterns.en: to get a good / bad grade

recap: Tira o casaco, senta-te e tira uma fotografia comigo! (Take off your coat, sit down and take a photo with me!)

intro: Criar means to create, but also to raise or bring up children and animals. It's a regular -ar verb: crio, crias, cria.

quick.en: I was raised by my grandmother.

presente.en: I keep chickens in the back yard.
Do you create your own games?
This factory creates lots of jobs.

presente.pt: Nós [criamos] os filhos com muito amor.
presente.en: We raise our children with lots of love.

presente.pt: Os avós [criam] os netos enquanto os pais trabalham.
presente.en: The grandparents bring up the grandchildren while the parents work.

perfeito.en: Have you created the password yet?
They set up a company in 2015.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era criança, [criava] histórias para o meu irmão.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to make up stories for my brother.
My uncle used to breed horses.
In the village, we used to keep rabbits.
My parents brought us up without television.

futuro.en: I'll create a website for the restaurant.
The new hospital will create a hundred jobs.
We'll create a group for the class.
Will you create the invitation for the party?

condicional.en: I would set up my own company.
Would you bring up your children in the countryside?
That would create problems.
We would create a garden here.

presente.pt: Estou a criar uma conta nova.

imperfeito.en: My grandparents kept chickens.
He used to create music.
We used to make up games.

futuro.en: I'm going to create a password.
The project will create jobs.
Are you going to create a website?

condicional.en: That would create confusion.
I would create something different.
Would you raise a dog in a flat?

notes.presente: Criar = to create, and also to raise or bring up (children, animals): criar os filhos, criar galinhas. Don't confuse with crescer (to grow up): Cresci no Porto.
notes.perfeito: Watch nós: criamos (presente) vs criámos (perfeito, with accent in EP).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou criar, vai criar.

compare.ex: Cresci numa aldeia perto de Braga.
Fiz um bolo para a festa.

recap: A minha avó criou seis filhos e ainda criou uma empresa! (My grandmother raised six children and still set up a company!)

intro: Nascer means to be born, and also to rise (the sun) or to start. It's a regular -er verb with a spelling change in eu: nasço. You'll use it mostly in the perfeito: Nasci em...

presente.pt: No verão, o sol [nasce] às seis.
presente.en: In summer, the sun rises at six.
Lots of babies are born in August.
You aren't born knowing how to speak.

perfeito.en: I was born in Lisbon in 1990.
The twins were born in March.

imperfeito.en: In the old days, children were born at home.

imperfeito.pt: O sol [nascia] quando saímos de casa.
imperfeito.en: The sun was rising when we left home.
Back then, we were all born in the village.

imperfeito.pt: Na aldeia, [nascia] um bebé por ano.
imperfeito.en: In the village, one baby was born a year.

futuro.en: The baby will be born in June.

futuro.pt: Os pintainhos [nascerão] daqui a uma semana.
futuro.en: The chicks will hatch in a week.

futuro.pt: Amanhã o sol [nascerá] às sete e um quarto.
futuro.en: Tomorrow the sun will rise at a quarter past seven.

futuro.pt: Daqui a uns anos, [nascerão] novas ideias.
futuro.en: In a few years, new ideas will be born.

condicional.en: If I could choose, I'd be born in the Algarve.
Where would you be born, if you could choose?

condicional.pt: Sem este hospital, o bebé não [nasceria] bem.
condicional.en: Without this hospital, the baby wouldn't be born safely.

condicional.pt: Sem esta lei, eles não [nasceriam] portugueses.
condicional.en: Without this law, they wouldn't be born Portuguese.

presente.en: The sun rises in the east.

imperfeito.en: The sun was rising.
Babies used to be born at home.
Few children were born in the village.

futuro.en: The baby is going to be born in May.
futuro.pt: O bebé vai nascer em maio.

futuro.en: When is the baby going to be born?
The sun is going to rise soon.
futuro.pt: O sol vai nascer daqui a pouco.

condicional.en: Where would you like to be born?
I would be born again!
Without water, nothing would be born.

notes.presente: Spelling change in eu only: nasço (c → ç before o). In English it's passive (to be born), but in Portuguese it's an ordinary verb: nasci = I was born. O sol nasce = the sun rises.
notes.perfeito: To say where and when you were born, always use the perfeito: Nasci em Lisboa, em 1990. Note nós nascemos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito for background or habits: O sol nascia (the sun was rising).
notes.futuro: In speech: vai nascer (is going to be born).

patterns.en: to be born in + place / year

compare.ex: Nasci em Lisboa, mas cresci no Porto.

recap: Nasci em Lisboa, mas o meu coração nasceu no Porto. (I was born in Lisbon, but my heart was born in Porto.)

intro: Viver means to live, both in the sense of living somewhere and of living your life. It's a regular -er verb. Morar is a common alternative for where you live.

presente.pt: Eu [vivo] em Lisboa há dois anos.
presente.en: I've been living in Lisbon for two years.
My parents live in the countryside.

perfeito.en: I lived in London for three years.

perfeito.pt: O meu avô [viveu] até aos cem anos.
perfeito.en: My grandfather lived to a hundred.
We had amazing moments on holiday.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I lived in a village.
He was still living with his parents.
We lived on a third floor with no lift.
They lived near us.

futuro.en: One day I'll live by the sea.
Who will you live with in Lisbon?
My brother will live with us.

futuro.pt: Os nossos filhos [viverão] melhor do que nós.
futuro.en: Our children will live better than us.

condicional.en: I would live in Porto.
Would you live in the countryside?
We would live better without so much rush.
They would live in Portugal, if they could.

perfeito.en: I lived in Spain for a year.
They lived there for ten years.

imperfeito.en: I used to live near here.
We lived in the centre.
Where did you live then?

futuro.en: I'm going to live in Portugal.
Are you going to live together?
She's going to live with us.

condicional.en: Would you live here?
I would live by the sea.
We would live in a smaller house.

notes.presente: Vivo em Lisboa há dois anos = I've been living in Lisbon for two years (presente + há, not a perfect tense). Morar also means to live (somewhere) and is very common: Moro no Porto.
notes.perfeito: Vivi três anos em Londres = a finished period. Note nós vivemos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Vivia em... = I used to live in... (background, no clear end).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou viver. Ir viver para = to move to (a place): Vou viver para Portugal.

compare.en: to live / to reside (only where you live)

recap: Vivo em Lisboa e vivo bem! (I live in Lisbon and I live well!)

intro: Morrer means to die. It's a regular -er verb. In everyday Portuguese it's very often used to exaggerate: morro de fome (I'm starving), morrer de rir (to die laughing).

presente.en: With this film, you'll die laughing.
Nobody dies from waiting a little.

presente.pt: No verão, [morremos] de calor nesta casa.
presente.en: In summer, we die of heat in this house.

perfeito.en: Many people died in the 1755 earthquake.
Did you get a terrible fright?

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu [morria] de medo do escuro.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I was terrified of the dark.

imperfeito.pt: O cão [morria] de saudades quando saíamos.
imperfeito.en: The dog missed us terribly when we went out.
We were dying of heat in the car.
The flowers always died in winter.

futuro.en: Without sun, the plant will die.
Tasting it won't kill you.
Without dinner, we'll starve!
The fish will die without oxygen.

condicional.en: I would die of embarrassment.
You would die of boredom there.
Without water, the dog would die.
We would miss you terribly.

perfeito.pt: O meu gato morreu no ano passado.

imperfeito.en: I was dying of thirst.
She was terrified of dogs.
imperfeito.pt: Ela morria de medo de cães.

imperfeito.en: We were dying of cold.

futuro.en: You're going to die laughing.
The plant is going to die.
It won't kill you! (You're not going to die)

condicional.en: I would die of fright.
She would die of shame.
Without you, I would die of boredom.

notes.presente: Morrer de + noun is an everyday exaggeration: morro de fome, morro de sono, morrer de rir. In EP: Estou a morrer de fome!
notes.perfeito: The participle is irregular: morto (dead): O peixe está morto. Faleceu is a polite, formal way to say someone died. Note nós morremos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Morria de medo de... = I used to be terrified of...
notes.futuro: In speech: vai morrer, vais morrer de rir.

patterns.en: to be starving / dying of thirst / dead tired

recap: Estou a morrer de fome, mas não vou morrer! (I'm starving, but I'm not going to die!)

intro: Matar means to kill. It's a regular -ar verb. In everyday Portuguese it's mostly figurative: matar a sede (to quench your thirst), matar o tempo (to kill time), matar saudades (to catch up with someone you've missed).

presente.pt: Eu [mato] a sede com água fresca.
presente.en: I quench my thirst with cold water.
Will you kill that fly, please?

presente.pt: [Matamos] o tempo a jogar às cartas.

perfeito.en: Did you get to see your family again?
We made up for lost time with a good salt cod.

imperfeito.pt: No comboio, [matava] o tempo a ler.
imperfeito.en: On the train, I used to kill time reading.
My cat used to kill birds.

imperfeito.pt: [Matávamos] a fome com pão e queijo.
imperfeito.en: We used to fill up on bread and cheese.

imperfeito.pt: No verão, os netos [matavam] saudades dos avós.
imperfeito.en: In summer, the grandchildren caught up with their grandparents.

futuro.en: I'll quench my thirst with a draught beer.
The poison will kill the ants.
In the Algarve, we'll make up for missing the sun.
Pesticides will kill the bees.

condicional.en: I would kill for a coffee!
You wouldn't hurt a fly.

condicional.pt: Um copo de água [mataria] a sede.
condicional.en: A glass of water would quench the thirst.
A visit would let them catch up.

perfeito.en: We caught up (we'd missed each other).

imperfeito.en: I used to kill time on my phone.
The dog used to kill chickens.
We quenched our thirst at the fountain.

futuro.en: I'm going to kill that mosquito!
We're going to catch up.
My mother is going to kill me!

condicional.en: I'd kill for a beer.
He wouldn't kill anyone.
That would kill the plant.

notes.presente: Very common figurative uses: matar a fome / a sede (satisfy hunger / thirst), matar o tempo (kill time), matar saudades (to see or enjoy again something you've missed).
notes.perfeito: European spelling: matámos (Brazil: matamos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou matar. A minha mãe vai matar-me! = I'm going to be in big trouble!
notes.condicional: Matava por... (imperfeito) is the casual way to say 'I'd kill for...' in EP.

patterns.en: to catch up / to make up for missing someone

compare.ex: A planta morreu com o frio.

recap: Vamos a Lisboa matar saudades e matar a fome com pastéis de nata! (Let's go to Lisbon to catch up and fill up on custard tarts!)

intro: Tomar means to take, but mostly in fixed uses: food and drink (tomar um café, tomar o pequeno-almoço), medicine, a shower (tomar banho) or a decision. It's a regular -ar verb.

quick.en: Shall we go for a coffee?
I'm going to have a shower.

presente.en: We have a drink after work.
They take the pill at dinner.

perfeito.en: We had breakfast at the hotel.

imperfeito.en: I always used to have tea in the afternoon.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [tomava] conta de nós.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather used to look after us.
We used to bathe in the river.
They took notes during class.

futuro.en: I'll make a decision tomorrow.
Will you look after the dog?

futuro.pt: O novo diretor [tomará] posse em janeiro.
futuro.en: The new director will take office in January.
Afterwards we'll have a coffee.

condicional.en: I would have a tea.
Would you look after the kids tomorrow?

condicional.pt: No lugar dele, eu... não, ele [tomaria] outro caminho.
condicional.en: In his place, I... no, he would take another route.
They would have breakfast with us.

imperfeito.en: I used to have coffee every morning.
She looked after her brother.
We used to take notes.

futuro.en: I'm going to have a shower.
Are you going to have breakfast?
Who's going to look after the cat?
futuro.pt: Quem vai tomar conta do gato?

condicional.en: I'd have a glass of wine.
condicional.pt: Eu tomava um copo de vinho.

condicional.en: Would you take that risk?
We would make a different decision.

notes.presente: Tomar is for meals and drinks (tomar um café, tomar o pequeno-almoço), medicine, showers (tomar banho, tomar um duche) and decisions. To catch a bus or train, EP uses apanhar: apanho o autocarro. To take something somewhere is levar.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: tomámos (Brazil: tomamos).
notes.imperfeito: Tomar conta de = to look after: tomava conta do irmão.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou tomar banho, vamos tomar um café.

patterns.en: to have a bath or shower

compare.ex: Levo o almoço para o trabalho.

recap: Tomo um duche, tomo o pequeno-almoço e apanho o autocarro. (I have a shower, have breakfast and catch the bus.)

intro: Ganhar means to win (a game, a prize) and also to earn (money) or to gain (time, weight, confidence). It's a regular -ar verb.

presente.pt: Eu [ganho] pouco, mas gosto do trabalho.
presente.en: I don't earn much, but I like the job.
How much do you earn a month?

presente.pt: O Benfica [ganha] quase sempre em casa.
presente.en: Benfica almost always win at home.
By train, we save an hour.

perfeito.en: I won a prize in the raffle!

imperfeito.en: In that job, I earned very little.

imperfeito.pt: O meu irmão [ganhava] sempre às cartas.
imperfeito.en: My brother always used to win at cards.
We used to win every game.

imperfeito.pt: Os meus avós [ganhavam] a vida a pescar.
imperfeito.en: My grandparents earned their living fishing.

futuro.en: In the new job, I'll earn more.
With practice, you'll gain confidence.
Who will win the election?
They will win the championship.

condicional.en: In Lisbon, I would earn more.
Self-employed, you would earn more.
By metro, we would save time.
They would win, if they played better.

imperfeito.en: He always used to win.
I earned less before.
They used to win every year.

futuro.en: We're going to win!
You're going to earn more.
Who's going to win?

condicional.en: I would win easily.
Would you earn more there?
We'd win with him.

notes.presente: Ganhar = to win (ganhar o jogo) and to earn (ganhar bem / mal). Ganhar tempo = to save time; ganhar peso = to put on weight.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: ganhámos (Brazil: ganhamos). Ganhar a + score: ganhámos por dois a zero.
notes.imperfeito: Ganhar a vida = to earn a living: ganhavam a vida a pescar.
notes.futuro: In speech: vamos ganhar! (we're going to win!).

compare.ex: Perdemos o jogo por um golo.

recap: Não ganho muito, mas hoje ganhei o jogo! (I don't earn much, but today I won the game!)

intro: Perder means to lose, and also to miss (a train, a chance, an event). It's irregular only in the eu form of the presente: perco. Perder-se means to get lost.

presente.en: You're not coming? You'll miss a great party!

presente.pt: O Sporting [perde] poucos jogos em casa.
presente.en: Sporting lose few games at home.
We waste a lot of time in traffic.

perfeito.en: I missed the eight o'clock bus.
They missed the flight to Paris.

imperfeito.en: I always used to lose at cards.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [perdia] as chaves todas as semanas.
imperfeito.en: He lost his keys every week.
We used to spend hours chatting.
They always used to miss the first train.

futuro.pt: Se não te despachares, [perderás] o comboio.
futuro.en: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the train.
I won't miss this opportunity.
Who will lose the game?

futuro.pt: [Perderemos] o voo, se não sairmos já.
futuro.en: We'll miss the flight if we don't leave now.

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [perderia] um jogo do Benfica.
condicional.en: I would never miss a Benfica game.
Would you lose your job over that?
Without help, he would lose everything.
By car, we would waste a lot of time.

presente.pt: Estás a perder o teu tempo.

imperfeito.en: He was always losing things.
We used to lose every game.
I used to get lost a lot.

futuro.en: You're going to miss the bus.
We're not going to lose!
I'm not going to miss this.

condicional.en: I would lose the bet.
You would get lost without a map.
They would lose a lot of money.

notes.presente: Only eu is irregular: perco (d → c). Perder = to lose and to miss (a train, a film, a chance). Perder tempo = to waste time. Não percas! = don't miss it!
notes.perfeito: Perder-se = to get lost: perdi-me no Porto. Note nós perdemos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Perdia sempre... = I always used to lose / miss...
notes.futuro: In speech: vais perder (you're going to miss/lose).
notes.condicional: Casual EP often uses the imperfeito instead: Sem mapa, perdias-te (you'd get lost).

patterns.en: to miss the train / the bus

recap: Perdi o comboio, perdi as chaves, mas não perdi o bom humor! (I missed the train, lost my keys, but didn't lose my good mood!)

intro: Andar means to walk or to move around, and also to ride (andar de bicicleta, de carro). It's a regular -ar verb. In European Portuguese, andar a + infinitive means 'to be doing (lately)'.

presente.pt: Eu [ando] a pé para o trabalho.
Eles [andam] a estudar para os exames.
presente.en: They've been studying for the exams.

perfeito.en: Have you ever been on a plane?

perfeito.pt: Ele [andou] de mota pela primeira vez.
perfeito.en: He rode a motorbike for the first time.
We walked all over the city.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [andava] de bicicleta todos os dias.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I rode my bike every day.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [andava] sempre de chapéu.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather always wore a hat.
We went to the same school.
They were looking for a house.

futuro.en: This year I'll walk more.
With these boots, you'll walk better.
The new train will go faster.
Tomorrow we'll go on a boat on the Tagus.

condicional.en: I would walk more if I had time.
Would you walk alone at night?

condicional.pt: Ele [andaria] de bicicleta, se houvesse ciclovias.
condicional.en: He would cycle if there were bike lanes.

condicional.pt: Eles [andariam] a pé até à praia.
condicional.en: They would walk to the beach.

presente.en: I've been reading a great book lately.
presente.pt: Ando a ler um livro ótimo.

imperfeito.en: She used to walk to school.
imperfeito.pt: Ela andava a pé para a escola.

imperfeito.en: I was looking for you.
We were in the same class.

futuro.en: I'm going to go for a walk.
We're going to ride bikes.
Are you going to go on the tram?

condicional.en: I would walk, but it's far.
Would you go on a boat?
She would walk more slowly.

notes.presente: Andar a + infinitivo = to have been doing lately: Ando a aprender português. Andar de + transport = to ride / to go by: andar de bicicleta, de autocarro. Andar + adjective = to have been (lately): ando cansado.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: andámos (Brazil: andamos). Por onde andaste? = Where have you been?
notes.imperfeito: Andar na escola = to go to school (attend): andávamos na mesma escola.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou andar, vamos andar de barco.

patterns.en: to walk / to go on foot
to ride a bike / go by car / fly

compare.ex: Vou a pé para a escola.

recap: Ando a aprender português e ando muito contente! (I've been learning Portuguese and I've been very happy!)

intro: Correr means to run. It's a regular -er verb. It also means 'to go' when talking about how something went: Como correu? Correu bem! (How did it go? It went well!)

presente.en: I run in the park at seven.
We run to catch the bus.
The children run on the beach.

perfeito.en: Did you run a lot today?
The kids ran to their mother.

imperfeito.en: I used to run five kilometres a day.
Everything was going well until the end.

imperfeito.pt: [Corríamos] na praia ao fim da tarde.
imperfeito.en: We used to run on the beach in the late afternoon.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [corriam] para casa quando começou a chover.
imperfeito.en: They were running home when it started to rain.

futuro.en: You'll see, everything will go well.
Will you run the half marathon?
Tomorrow we'll run together.
Next time, I'll run more slowly.

condicional.pt: Eu [correria], mas tenho o joelho mal.
condicional.en: I would run, but my knee is bad.
Would you run a marathon?

condicional.pt: Com outro chefe, o projeto [correria] melhor.
condicional.en: With another boss, the project would go better.
We would run more if we had time.

presente.pt: Estou a correr para a estação.

perfeito.en: We ran all the way home.

imperfeito.en: I used to run every morning.
Things were going well.
The dog was running after the cat.
imperfeito.pt: O cão corria atrás do gato.

futuro.en: I'm going to go for a run.
It's going to go well.
Are you going to run tomorrow?

condicional.en: I would run faster.
It would go badly.
Would you run in this heat?

notes.presente: Besides 'to run', correr means 'to go' for events: Como correu o exame? Correu bem. Correr atrás de = to run after.
notes.perfeito: Como correu? / Correu bem! is one of the most useful phrases in EP. Note nós corremos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Tudo corria bem = everything was going well (background).
notes.futuro: In speech: vai correr bem (it'll go well), a common reassurance.

compare.ex: Ando a pé para o trabalho.

recap: Corri para apanhar o comboio e correu tudo bem! (I ran to catch the train and everything went well!)

intro: Nadar means to swim. It's a regular -ar verb. For a casual dip in the sea, people often say tomar banho or dar um mergulho instead.

presente.pt: Eu [nado] na piscina duas vezes por semana.
presente.en: I swim in the pool twice a week.
My son already swims on his own.
In summer, we swim in the sea.
The dolphins swim near the boat.

perfeito.en: Did you swim in the river?
He swam out to the buoy.
We swam in Sesimbra on Saturday.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I swam every day.
My father was a very good swimmer.
We used to swim in the village lake.
They were swimming while we were reading.

futuro.en: Tomorrow I'll swim in the sea.
With lessons, you'll be swimming in no time.
He will swim at the Olympic Games.
We'll swim in the hotel pool.

condicional.pt: Eu [nadaria], mas a água está fria.
condicional.en: I would swim, but the water is cold.
Would you swim in the Atlantic in January?

condicional.pt: [Nadaríamos] todos os dias, se houvesse piscina.
condicional.en: We would swim every day if there were a pool.
They would swim more if they had time.

presente.pt: Ela está a nadar no mar.

imperfeito.en: I used to swim a lot.
We swam every summer.
He couldn't swim well.

futuro.en: I'm going to swim.
Are you going to swim in the sea?
We're going to swim tomorrow.

condicional.en: I wouldn't swim here.
Would you swim with sharks?
She would swim faster.

notes.presente: Sabes nadar? = Can you swim? (know how). Use saber for skills, not poder. For a quick dip in the sea: tomar banho no mar or dar um mergulho.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: nadámos (Brazil: nadamos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou nadar, vamos nadar.

patterns.en: to swim in the sea / in the pool

compare.en: to go for a dip / to bathe

recap: Não sei nadar bem, mas adoro tomar banho no mar. (I can't swim well, but I love bathing in the sea.)

intro: Voar means to fly. It's a regular -ar verb: voo, voas, voa. Like in English, o tempo voa (time flies).

presente.en: Which airline are you flying with?
The seagulls fly over the river.

perfeito.en: I flew from Lisbon to Madeira.
The bird flew into the tree.

imperfeito.en: I used to fly a lot for work.
The plane was flying very low.

imperfeito.pt: [Voávamos] sempre à noite, porque era mais barato.
imperfeito.en: We always flew at night because it was cheaper.

imperfeito.pt: Os papagaios de papel [voavam] na praia.
imperfeito.en: The kites were flying on the beach.

futuro.en: I'll fly to London on Monday.
Will you fly business class?

futuro.pt: O avião [voará] a dez mil metros.
futuro.en: The plane will fly at ten thousand metres.
We'll fly direct to the Azores.

condicional.en: If I could, I would fly like a bird.
Would you fly in such a small plane?

condicional.pt: Ele [voaria] para o Brasil, se o bilhete fosse barato.
condicional.en: He would fly to Brazil if the ticket were cheap.

condicional.pt: [Voaríamos] de manhã, mas é mais caro.
condicional.en: We would fly in the morning, but it's more expensive.

perfeito.en: We flew with a cheap airline.

imperfeito.en: The plane was flying over the sea.
imperfeito.pt: O avião voava sobre o mar.

imperfeito.en: I used to fly every month.
The days flew by.

futuro.en: I'm going to fly to Lisbon.
We're going to fly tomorrow.
Are you going to fly or drive?
futuro.pt: Vais de avião ou de carro?

condicional.en: I would never fly with them.
Would you like to fly?
It would fly better.

notes.presente: Eu voo: no circumflex in current spelling (the old spelling was vôo). O voo also means 'the flight': O voo está atrasado.
notes.perfeito: Ele voou (two o's). European spelling: voámos (Brazil: voamos).
notes.futuro: In speech, people often say ir de avião instead of voar: Vou de avião para Londres.

compare.ex: Vamos de avião para os Açores.

recap: O voo foi curto: voámos para o Porto e o tempo voou! (The flight was short: we flew to Porto and the time flew!)

intro: Pedir means to ask for something: food in a restaurant, help, a favour, money. It's irregular only in eu: peço. Don't confuse it with perguntar, which is asking a question.

presente.en: What are you ordering for dinner?
Shall we ask for the bill?

presente.pt: Os miúdos [pedem] gelado todos os dias.
presente.en: The kids ask for ice cream every day.

perfeito.pt: [Pedi] um café e um pastel de nata.
perfeito.en: I ordered a coffee and a custard tart.
Have you asked for the bill?
She asked me for help with the suitcases.
We asked for information at reception.

imperfeito.en: I always used to order the same thing.

imperfeito.pt: O meu filho [pedia] para ficar acordado.
imperfeito.en: My son used to ask to stay up.
On Saturdays we used to order pizza.
They used to borrow money from friends.

futuro.en: I'll ask my boss for a pay rise.
Will you ask for help if you need it?
The receptionist will ask for your passport.
They will ask for more time.

condicional.en: I would order the fish.
What would you order?
He would never ask anyone for money.

condicional.pt: [Pediríamos] outra garrafa, mas já é tarde.
condicional.en: We would order another bottle, but it's already late.

presente.en: I'm going to order now. (I'll order now.)

perfeito.en: Did you ask for the bill?

imperfeito.en: She always ordered dessert.
We used to ask for advice.
I never asked for anything.

futuro.en: I'm going to ask for the bill.
Are you going to ask him for help?
We're going to order a pizza.

condicional.en: I'd order the steak.
Would you ask for a discount?
They would ask for more money.

notes.presente: Only eu is irregular: peço (like medir → meço, ouvir → ouço). Pedir = ask FOR something (a thing, food, help, a favour). Peço desculpa is the standard EP 'sorry'.
notes.perfeito: Pedir a alguém para + infinitivo = to ask someone to do something: Pediu-me para esperar. Note nós pedimos is the same in presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Pedir emprestado = to borrow: pediam dinheiro emprestado.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou pedir a conta, vamos pedir.

patterns.en: to ask someone to do something

recap: Pedi a conta e perguntei se podia pagar com cartão. (I asked for the bill and asked if I could pay by card.)

intro: Perguntar means to ask a question or ask for information. It's a regular -ar verb. If you're asking FOR something (an object, a favour), use pedir instead.

presente.pt: Eu [pergunto] ao professor depois da aula.
presente.en: I'll ask the teacher after class.
He asks where the station is.
Shall we ask someone the way?

perfeito.pt: [Perguntei] o preço, mas era muito caro.
perfeito.en: I asked the price, but it was too expensive.
Did you ask what time it opens?

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [perguntava] tudo aos meus pais.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I asked my parents about everything.
He always used to ask the same thing.

imperfeito.pt: [Perguntávamos] a toda a gente, mas ninguém sabia.
imperfeito.en: We asked everyone, but nobody knew.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [perguntavam] por ti todos os dias.
imperfeito.en: They asked after you every day.

futuro.en: I'll ask the doctor.
Will you ask your mother?
The police officer will ask your name.
The students will ask about everything.

condicional.en: I would ask a local.
Would you ask the price first?
He would never ask that.
We would ask, but there's nobody here.

perfeito.en: I asked where the bathroom was.
perfeito.pt: Perguntei onde era a casa de banho.

imperfeito.en: He always asked a lot of questions.
I never used to ask.
They kept asking about the price.

futuro.en: I'm going to ask the teacher.
Are you going to ask her?
We're going to ask the way.

condicional.en: I would ask first.
Would you ask him?
Nobody would ask that.

notes.presente: Perguntar = to ask a question or for information: Pergunto onde é a estação. Perguntar a alguém = to ask someone. Perguntar por alguém = to ask after someone. Fazer uma pergunta = to ask a question.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: perguntámos (Brazil: perguntamos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou perguntar.

recap: Perguntei ao empregado o que era bom e pedi o bacalhau. (I asked the waiter what was good and ordered the salt cod.)
